extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians working in arithmetic geometry/anabelian geometry and readers of Inter-Universal Teichmüller theory (IUT)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, constructions, and compatibility conditions for radial/coric/multiradial environments and for cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms arising from functorial group-theoretic algorithms in the IUT framework. Focuses on what structure/data must be present and how indeterminacies (Aut(G), Γ, torsion quotients) propagate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radial algorithm determines multiradial environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The radial algorithm given by the assignment (Π MTM(Π), G O×μ(G), α,×μ) → (G O×μ(G)) — whose associated radial functor is full and essentially surjective, hence determines a multiradial environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A radial algorithm determines a multiradial environment precisely when its associated radial functor is full and essentially surjective; checking fullness and essential surjectivity is the decisive condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of radial data (Example 1.8 (viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection of radial data consists of the output data of the algorithm of (∗TM) associated to a topological group Π isomorphic to Π^tp_X, the output data of the second algorithm (∗_gp) associated to a topological group G isomorphic to G_k, and a diagram α,×μ of poly-morphisms of ind-topological monoids equipped with topological group actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Radial data must include the concrete outputs of the specified functorial/group-theoretic algorithms for Π and G together with the poly-morphism diagram α(−) that relates the two; omitting any of these components means the 'radial data' is not as defined here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism of collections of radial data
rubrics_metrics.description: An isomorphism of collections of radial data consists of (i) an isomorphism of ind-topological monoids with topological group actions induced by an isomorphism Π ≅ Π*, and (ii) a Γ-multiple of the isomorphism of ind-topological modules with topological group actions induced by an isomorphism G ≅ G*; these isomorphisms must be compatible with the poly-morphism α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compatibility with the α-diagram is required; such an isomorphism induces compatible isomorphisms on the various O×, O×μ, and related objects appearing in the radial data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-shell version (Example 1.8 (ix))
rubrics_metrics.description: If G ≅ G_k, one may construct the log-shell I(G) ⊆ O×μ(G) (p^−1 times the image of the G-invariants of O×(G) in O×μ(G)); replacing the notation G O×μ(G) by (G O×μ(G), I(G) ⊆ O×μ(G)) yields a 'log-shell version' of the multiradial environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the log-shell I(G) equips O×μ(G) with additional substructure; doing so produces a variant of the multiradial environment and must be accounted for in definitions and compatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automorphism coincidence (Remark 1.8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the examples considered, no automorphism of O×μ(G) induced by an element of Aut(G) (e.g., inner automorphisms from G) coincides with an automorphism induced by an element of Γ whose image in Z_p^× is nontrivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from the natural surjection O×μ(G) → Q_p obtained via the p-adic logarithm of the cyclotomic character, which is Aut(G)-equivariant (Aut(G) acts trivially on Q_p) and Γ-equivariant (Γ acts via the cyclotomic character). Use this test to distinguish Aut(G)-induced vs Γ-induced automorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph construction of a functorial algorithm (Example 1.9 (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given categories E, F and a functor Ξ : E → F arising from a functorial algorithm, the graph category G has objects (E, Ξ(E)) and morphisms (f: E → E', Ξ(f): Ξ(E) → Ξ(E')). Natural functors E → G, G → E, and G → F exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'graph' construction is a canonical way to package input-output pairs of a functorial algorithm and is used to define the category R† when applied to radial environments; ensure morphisms are paired accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautological multiradialization (Example 1.9 (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Composing the functor R → E (sending (Π,G,α) ↦ Π) with Ξ : E → F yields R → F; its graph R† and natural functor Ψ_R : R → R† are multiradially defined. Any functorial group-theoretic algorithm with input a topological group Π ≅ Π^tp_X gives rise tautologically to a multiradially defined functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the 'tautological' or 'general nonsense' approach: forming graphs of algorithms gives multiradial definitions in a natural, but often uninteresting, way; use when a tautological multiradialization is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniradial construction (Example 1.9 (iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Defining radial data simply as a topological group Π (isomorphic to Π^tp_X) and taking isomorphisms of radial data to be isomorphisms of topological groups yields a radial functor Φ that fails to be full; (R,C,Φ) is a uniradial environment and Ψ_R is uniradially defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniradial functors depend strictly on the arithmetic holomorphic structure and typically only allow consistent execution on one 'spoke' at a time; do not expect simultaneous multi-spoke compatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daggered radial data (Example 1.9 (iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection of daggered radial data consists of radial data (Π,G,α) together with the poly-isomorphism (l·ΔΘ)(Π) → μ_Z(G) obtained by composing the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism with the poly-isomorphism induced by α. An isomorphism of daggered radial data must be compatible with this final poly-isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daggered radial data strengthen radial data by adding the cyclotomic/θ-module poly-isomorphism; compatibility of isomorphisms must include this datum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual taxonomy: uniradial, coric, multiradial (Remark 1.9.1/1.9.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniradially defined functors correspond to constructions depending strictly on the arithmetic holomorphic structure; corically defined functors depend only on the underlying mono-analytic (real analytic) structure; multiradially defined functors depend on the arithmetic holomorphic structure but in a way compatible with how that structure is related to the mono-analytic core (via the α poly-morphisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this taxonomy to classify constructions: check dependence on arithmetic holomorphic structure and whether compatibility descriptions (embeddings into mono-analytic structure) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity via functorial algorithms (Corollary 1.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: By composing the functorial algorithm Π → M_Θ^*(Π) with the algorithm constructing a cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism, one obtains an isomorphism (l·ΔΘ)(Π) ∼→ Π_μ(M_Θ^*(Π)); the resulting data determine a functor R → F arising from a functorial algorithm in Π and Ψ_R is multiradially defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To produce the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism used in multiradial constructions, follow the specified composition of algorithms; verify the constructions of domain and codomain from the mono-theta environment and the theta-section images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict cyclotomic rigidity compatibility with coricity (Remark 1.10.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because O×μ(G) is formed from O×(G) by quotienting by roots of unity, and because the homomorphism Π_μ(M_Θ^*(Π)) ⊗ Q/Z → O×μ(G) is trivial in the mono-theta context, any rigidification of Π_μ(M_Θ^*(Π)) depending only on the mono-theta-environment will be tautologically compatible with the coricity of O×μ(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rigidity depends only on mono-theta data, it will automatically respect coricity (sharing of O×μ among arithmetic holomorphic structures); use this fact to distinguish situations of 'strict' rigidity from those with indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial cyclotomic rigidity with indeterminacies (Corollary 1.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider (a) the Γ-orbit of the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism μ_Z(G) ∼→ μ_Z(O×(G)) obtained from the MLF-Galois pair algorithm, and (b) the Aut(G)-orbit of isomorphisms μ_Z(G) ∼→ (l·ΔΘ)(Π) obtained via α; the triple (Π,G,α) together with these orbits and associated modules determines a functor R → F from a functorial algorithm in (Π,G,α) and yields Ψ_R multiradially defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This corollary formalizes that cyclotomic rigidity may appear only up to specified Γ- and Aut(G)-orbits (indeterminacies); when constructing/gluing such isomorphisms, track these orbit actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphism-group mapping and kernel descriptions (Remark 1.11.1 (i)(a–c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The automorphism group of the underlying MLF-Galois TM-pair of G O(cid:2)(G) maps bijectively onto Aut(G); the automorphism group of the underlying MLF-Galois TCG-pair of G O×(G) maps surjectively onto Aut(G) with kernel given by the G-linear automorphisms of O×(G) determined by the natural (Z^×)-action; similarly for O (cid:9)gp(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing indeterminacies, use these precise descriptions: indeterminacies on the module objects correspond to (Z^×)-actions and appear as kernels when forgetting the O(−) structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisibility and Q_p-action on O×μ(G) (Remark 1.11.1 (i)(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The underlying ind-topological module of O×μ(G) is divisible and therefore admits a natural action by Q_p; consequently, the kernel description applicable to O×(G) (involving (Z^×)-action) does not hold for O×μ(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because O×μ(G) is divisible, its automorphism/indeterminacy behavior differs: do not import kernel descriptions from O×(G) naively when working with O×μ(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of passing to O×μ for certain multiradial constructions (Remark 1.11.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: To construct certain multiradially defined functors important in the theory, one must form the quotient of O×(−) by its torsion subgroup (i.e., work with O×μ(−)) rather than with O×(−); gluing across distinct Θ-Hodge theaters is possible up to an (Aut(G), Γ)-indeterminacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning multiradial gluing or rigidity constructions, check whether torsion must be factored out; doing so changes the permissible indeterminacies and makes consistent gluing possible only up to the stated (Aut, Γ)-orbit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of coric data and effect of forgetting anabelian structure (Remark 1.11.3 (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The radial functor specification (which portion of radial data one takes as coric data) matters: coric data should include Π → Π/Δ ≅ G; once one forgets the anabelian structure of objects constructed group-theoretically from Π or G, those objects no longer automatically constitute coric data and must be specified explicitly if they are to be treated as coric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about which objects are included in coric data; forgetting anabelian origins removes the canonical identification and forces explicit inclusion to enable gluing/identification operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propagation of indeterminacies via compatibility maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Compatibility with the natural maps O (cid:9)gp(G) ← O×(G) → O×μ(G) implies that an (Aut(G), Γ)-indeterminacy on G O×μ(G) induces corresponding (Aut(G), Γ)-indeterminacies on G O×(G) and G O (cid:9)gp(G); these induced indeterminacies are the orbits appearing in Corollary 1.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When tracing orbits/indeterminacies, follow the compatibility maps between the various O(−) objects: indeterminacies on the quotient O×μ propagate to the upstream O× and Ogp objects and must be accounted for.
